title: DS-160 Photo Requirements 2026: Digital US Visa Specs
metaDescription: Official DS-160 and DV lottery photo specs: square JPEG, 600x600 to 1200x1200 px, max 240 KB, white background, no glasses. Plus upload error fixes.
h1: DS-160 Photo Requirements 2026: Digital US Visa Specs
h1Subtitle: Official file, size and composition rules for DS-160, DS-260 and DV lottery photos
content:
Last updated: November 24, 2026. Every rule below comes from the U.S. Department of State's Photo Requirements and Digital Image Requirements pages, plus the Diversity Visa instructions.

If you are filling in a DS-160 (nonimmigrant visa), a DS-260 (immigrant visa) or a DV lottery entry, you need a digital photo that meets the State Department's file rules and its composition rules. This page covers both, explains how the three forms differ, and shows you how to fix the most common upload problems.

Quick answer: the digital file specs

For the DS-160 upload, your photo file must meet all of these:

RequirementOfficial spec
File formatJPEG (.jpg)
Minimum dimensions600 x 600 pixels
Maximum dimensions1200 x 1200 pixels
Aspect ratioSquare (height must equal width)
File size240 kB or less
ColourColour, 24 bits per pixel, sRGB colour space
CompressionCompression ratio of 20:1 or less
Scanned prints2 x 2 inch (51 x 51 mm) photo scanned at 300 pixels per inch

Source: Digital Image Requirements, travel.state.gov.

Make your US visa photo (600 x 600 px)

Composition rules: head size, eyes and background

A file can pass every technical check and still be refused if the face is framed wrongly. The State Department's Photo Composition Template sets these limits:

  • Head size: from the bottom of the chin to the top of the hair, the head must be 50% to 69% of the image height. On a 600 x 600 image that is 300 to 414 pixels. On a printed photo it is 1 to 1 3/8 inches (25 to 35 mm).
  • Eye height: measured from the bottom of the image to the eyes, between 56% and 69% of the image height. On a 600 x 600 image that is 336 to 414 pixels from the bottom.
  • Pose: full face, looking straight at the camera, neutral expression, both eyes open.
  • Background: plain white or off-white, with no patterns, objects or other people.
  • Colour and editing: the photo must be in colour and must not be digitally changed to alter your appearance. Filters and beauty apps are a risk.

Glasses, head coverings and clothing

  • Glasses: not allowed in new visa photos. The rare medical exception (for example, after eye surgery) needs a signed medical statement, and the frames still must not cover your eyes. The DV instructions simply say not to wear eyeglasses.
  • Hats and head coverings: only allowed if worn daily for religious reasons, and your full face must still be visible.
  • Headphones and devices: remove headphones and wireless hands-free devices.
  • Uniforms: do not wear one, except religious clothing worn every day.

How recent the photo must be

The photo must have been taken within the last 6 months and show how you look today. If your appearance has changed, take a new one. Photos copied or scanned from a driver's licence or other official document are not accepted.

DS-160 vs DS-260 vs DV lottery

ApplicationHow the photo is usedKey differences
DS-160 (nonimmigrant, e.g. B1/B2, F-1, H-1B)Uploaded online inside the formSquare JPEG, 600 x 600 to 1200 x 1200 px, 240 kB max. If the upload fails, bring one printed photo to the interview.
DS-260 (immigrant visa)Printed photos taken to the interviewBring two identical 2 x 2 inch colour photos. Your embassy may add its own instructions.
DV lottery entryUploaded with the online entrySquare JPEG, 600 x 600 px, 240 kB max, no glasses. A photo used in a previous year's entry makes you ineligible.

The DV rules are the strictest. According to the DV-2026 instructions, a photo that does not meet the specs, or that has been manipulated in any way, may make you ineligible. Always read the instructions for the current DV year before you enter. Our DV lottery photo checker is built for that entry.

Common upload errors and how to fix them

  • File too large: lower the JPEG quality or the pixel size until the file is 240 kB or less. Do not go below 600 x 600 px.
  • Image too small: retake or rescan the photo. Enlarging a small image adds blur and will not fix it.
  • Not square: crop to equal width and height, keeping the head at 50% to 69% of the height.
  • Wrong format: phones often save HEIC or PNG files. Export as JPEG.
  • Black-and-white or greyscale: use a colour sRGB image.
  • Face or background rejected: retake with even light, no shadows behind you, no glasses and a plain white or off-white wall.

The official Photo FAQ and DS-160 FAQ explain what to do if a photo keeps failing.

How to resize and compress the photo correctly

  1. Start with a sharp, well-lit original that is larger than 600 x 600 px.
  2. Crop to a square so the head fills 50% to 69% of the height and the eyes sit 56% to 69% up from the bottom.
  3. Resize to between 600 x 600 and 1200 x 1200 px. 600 x 600 meets every form, including the DV entry.
  4. Save as JPEG in sRGB colour and check the size. If it is over 240 kB, lower the quality a little and save again. Keep the compression at 20:1 or less so the face stays sharp.
  5. Do not use filters, smoothing or background effects that change how you look.

Our US visa photo editor handles the crop, the white background, the 600 x 600 px export and the 240 kB limit in one step.

How to check your photo before you submit

  • Open the file's details and confirm: JPEG, square, 600 to 1200 px per side, 240 kB or less.
  • Measure the head and eye height against the percentages above, or run it through our free visa photo checker.
  • Check the background, lighting and expression against the official template.
  • After you upload, look at the DS-160 confirmation page. If your photo shows there, the upload worked.

Applying for a green card instead? See our green card photo checker. For a longer guide to printed sizes and backgrounds, read US visa photo requirements: size, background and DS-160 rules.

Final acceptance of any photo is up to the U.S. embassy or consulate that handles your application. No tool can guarantee acceptance, so always check your embassy's own instructions.

Frequently asked questions

What size should a DS-160 photo be in pixels?

The image must be square, at least 600 x 600 pixels and no more than 1200 x 1200 pixels. Anything in between is fine as long as width and height are equal.

What is the maximum file size for a US visa photo?

240 kB. The file must be a JPEG (.jpg) of 240 kB or less. The State Department does not publish a minimum file size for the visa upload.

What happens if my DS-160 photo upload fails?

You can still submit the DS-160. The State Department says that if your confirmation page does not show your photo, you should bring one printed 2 x 2 inch photo with the confirmation page to your interview. Check your embassy's instructions too.

Can I wear glasses in a US visa photo?

No. Glasses are no longer allowed in new visa photos. The only exception is a rare medical case, such as recent eye surgery, and you must include a signed medical statement. The DV lottery instructions simply say not to wear eyeglasses.

Is the DV lottery photo the same as the DS-160 photo?

The composition rules are the same, but the DV instructions list the file as exactly 600 x 600 pixels, JPEG, 240 kB or less. You also cannot reuse a photo from a previous year's DV entry.

How recent does a US visa photo need to be?

It must have been taken within the last 6 months and show how you look now. Take a new photo if your appearance has changed, even if your old one is newer than 6 months.

Can I take a US visa photo with my phone?

The State Department says low-resolution mobile phone photos are not acceptable. What matters is the final file: sharp, in focus, correctly lit, on a plain white or off-white background, and within the pixel and file size limits.

Do I need a printed photo for my visa interview?

Not if your DS-160 upload worked and the photo shows on your confirmation page, although some embassies still ask for one. Immigrant visa applicants (DS-260) are told to bring two identical 2 x 2 inch printed photos to the interview.
